finding.claim: Unauthenticated remote code execution via Ruby Marshal deserialization of attacker-supplied data in POST /restore.
finding.source: params[:state] (app.rb:6), taken from the HTTP request query string or form body. No authentication is defined in app.rb.
finding.sink: Marshal.load (app.rb:6). Marshal can instantiate arbitrary objects and trigger gadget chains during load, which can run arbitrary code in the server process.

trace.note: POST /restore route is registered with no auth filter, before_filter, or content check.
params[:state] goes to Base64.decode64 with no validation, and the result goes directly to Marshal.load.
The deserialized object is returned via state.inspect, so the response also reflects the object's inspect output to the caller.

finding.guards_checked: No authentication or authorization on the route. No signature or HMAC on the state blob. No type allowlist. No size limit. No error handling around Base64 decode. No middleware, config, or test file in the repo adds any of these controls.

verdict.guard_found: none. app.rb:5 registers POST /restore with no before filter, auth, or content check. app.rb:6 passes params[:state] through Base64.decode64 straight into Marshal.load with no HMAC, type allowlist, or size limit. No other files exist in the repo (Glob returned only app.rb), so no middleware or config adds a control.
verdict.reason: The route at app.rb:5 is anonymous and app.rb:6 calls Marshal.load on attacker-controlled params[:state] with no effective guard, so anyone can reach the unsafe deserialization sink. Exploitability to code execution still depends on which gadget classes are loaded in the server process, which the repo alone cannot show, but the sink and the missing control are as described.

finding.claim: Unauthenticated POST /import accepts arbitrary JSON with no size limit and no type check before calling methods on the parsed value.
finding.source: request.body.read (app.rb:11), the raw HTTP body from any remote client.
finding.sink: data.keys (app.rb:12). Not a security sink; impact is a 500 crash or request-size resource cost.

trace.note: Raw body is read and parsed with JSON.parse. No size cap and no auth.
data.keys raises NoMethodError if the parsed JSON is an Array, String, Number, or null. The response is an error page, not an injection.

finding.guards_checked: No authentication. No Content-Type check. No rescue around parse or the method call. Output is data.keys.join, which only receives strings from a Hash, so there is no response injection. Low severity: robustness and DoS surface, not an exploitable injection.

verdict.guard_found: none. app.rb is the only file in the directory, so there is no auth filter, Rack middleware, body-size limit, or rescue. Lines 10-12 have no guard: the route is anonymous, and the body goes straight into JSON.parse (app.rb:11) and then data.keys (app.rb:12).
verdict.reason: At app.rb:11-12, an anonymous POST with a non-object JSON body (array, string, number, or null) makes data.keys raise NoMethodError, which returns a 500; the claim is accurate, but the impact is low robustness and resource cost, not an injection.
